basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 14.' and it opens 'Vers. 14. Fiant luminaria in firmamento coeli. Luminaria solem, et lunam, et caeteras'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 14. Fiant luminaria in firmamento coeli. Luminaria solem, et lunam, et caeteras stellas accipimus. Verum sol et luna et septem planetae non sunt in firmamento positae, sed in aethere pendent: ideo in firmamento positae dicuntur. Et dividant diem ac noctem. Sol diei praeest, luna nocti. Sint in signa. Hoc, vel propter terminum Paschalem dicitur, quia luna signum est Paschalis termini qui non nisi post quatuordecimam lunam celebratur, vel quia sidera signa sunt navigantibus per mare vel iter agentibus per Libyam ubi vestigium itineris ad | motum venti dissipatur. Luna apud Hebraeos tribus nominibus nuncupatur, Lare, Lavana, Mavors. Lara vocatur a numero dierum mensis: Lavana a candiditate: Mavors a defectu, quia deficit singulis mensibus.
